Skim-RTI / BrB-RTI / nilHMM — ancestry concordance on pedigree-matched NILs

Author

Fausto Rodríguez-Zapata

Published

June 25, 2026

Repo: sawers-rellan-labs/zealtiger

Skim-RTI, BrB-RTI, and nilHMM ancestry concordance, matched by NIL pedigree string — not by the PN#_SID# plate index, which is mislabeled in the BRB-seq run (docs/brbseq-sample-mislabeling.md, docs/brbseq_sample_identity.html). The BRB-seq plate id does not track the NIL; the pedigree string is the cross-experiment identifier. The only formatting difference between the two metadata files is a trailing .B the MolBreeding/skim registry appends and the BRB metadata omits, so we drop .B before joining.

  • BrB-RTI sample identity: BRBseq_metadata.csv (sample_id → genotype, drop .B).
  • Skim-RTI sample identity: the BZea registry (sample_metatada.csv → staged as data/skim_sample_pedigree.csv, already .B-dropped).
  • nilHMM: the same SNP50K skim reads as Skim-RTI, called by the nNIL count-based BetaBinomial HMM (nilhmm, FORMAT/AD; per-taxon r calibrated to the BC2S2 sim) — keyed on the skim sample name, so it adds a second skim caller alongside Skim-RTI. (At ~0.4× it is het-biased; read its donor footprint, not the HET/ALT split.)

The pedigree-matched pairs are sourced from the curated correspondence (results/sample_correspondence/skim_brbseq_correspondence.csv, built by sample_correspondence.qmd); this doc keeps the pairs whose ancestry calls are available here. (The coverage section below still pairs the full dataset directly via the registries.)

The per-NIL painting / confusion / Jaccard cover the 4 NILs that have both MolBreeding-GBTS and BRB-seq (pedigree-matched: Zv.0080, Zx.0340, Zx.0540, Zd.0030) — the lines with the most cross-platform support. The coverage and introgression-size sections use the full skim∩BRB set. (The earlier 8 PN4_SID# samples were a cross-id-space mislabeling artifact, not genuine MolBreeding∩BRB NILs — see docs/brbseq-sample-mislabeling.md.)

Setup

Code 
library(tidyverse); library(data.table); library(GenomicRanges); library(ggpubr)
pal <- c(REF = "gold", HET = "springgreen4", ALT = "purple4")
chop <- function(x) sub("\\.B$", "", x)

brb  <- read_csv(params$brb_taxa,   show_col_types = FALSE)   # BrB-RTI, per-species fit (carries the real BRB sample names)
skim <- read_csv(params$skim_calls, show_col_types = FALSE)
nilhmm <- read_csv(params$nilhmm,   show_col_types = FALSE)   # nilHMM (counts), keyed on skim sample name
nilhmm_chk <- read_csv(params$nilhmm_chk, show_col_types = FALSE)  # nilHMM B73/Purple checks
brbmeta <- read_csv(params$brb_meta, show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  transmute(sid = sample_id, nil = chop(genotype))
skimped <- read_csv(params$skim_ped, show_col_types = FALSE)   # sample, pedigree (.B-dropped)
corr <- read_csv(params$corr, show_col_types = FALSE) %>% filter(type == "NIL")  # full skim<->BRB map (intro-size section)

# Per-NIL painting / confusion / Jaccard scope = the MolBreeding-GBTS NILs that ALSO have
# BRB-seq, matched BY PEDIGREE (molbreeding_3way_correspondence.csv, in_brbseq == TRUE).
# Their real BRB libraries are PN3_SID265 / PN2_SID137 / PN1_SID10 / PN2_SID169 — NOT the
# PN4 plate names, which are a cross-id-space mislabeling artifact
# (docs/brbseq-sample-mislabeling.md). BrB-RTI calls come from the per-species fit (`brb`).
matched <- read_csv(params$molb_3way, show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  filter(type == "NIL", in_brbseq) %>%
  transmute(nil = molb_ped, skim_name = skim_prefix, brb_name = brbseq_prefix)

# common wideseq grid + state-on-grid
cf   <- read_tsv(list.files(params$mb_counts, full.names = TRUE)[1],
                 col_names = c("chr_label","bp","rb","rc","ab","ac"), show_col_types = FALSE)
grid <- tibble(chr = as.integer(sub("chr","",cf$chr_label)), bp = cf$bp)
gg   <- GRanges(grid$chr, IRanges(grid$bp, width = 1))
state_on_grid <- function(seg, nm) {
  d <- seg[seg$name == nm, ]
  d$state[findOverlaps(gg, GRanges(d$chr, IRanges(d$start_bp, d$end_bp)), select = "first")]
}

cat(sprintf("Per-NIL scope — MolBreeding NILs that also have BRB-seq (pedigree-matched): %d\n  %s\n",
            nrow(matched), paste(matched$nil, collapse = ", ")))

Coverage by platform — full dataset

Mean per-sample sequencing coverage on each platform, paired by NIL pedigree across the whole dataset (every BRB-seq sample joined to its same-pedigree skim sample). SNP50K-skim λ from real_skim_lambda.csv (mean depth over the 50K grid); BRB-seq λ from brbseq_coverage.csv (mean depth over the brbseq SNP sites). One point = one NIL. The mean of each platform is drawn as a dotted reference line.

Code 
brb_cov <- read_csv(params$brb_cov, show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(sid = as.integer(sub(".*_SID", "", name)),
         nil = brbmeta$nil[match(sid, brbmeta$sid)]) %>%
  filter(!is.na(nil)) %>% transmute(nil, brb_name = name, brb_cov = lambda)
skim_cov <- read_csv(params$skim_cov, show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(nil = skimped$pedigree[match(name, skimped$sample)]) %>%
  filter(!is.na(nil)) %>%
  group_by(nil) %>% summarise(skim_name = dplyr::first(name), skim_cov = dplyr::first(lambda), .groups = "drop")
cov <- inner_join(brb_cov, skim_cov, by = "nil") %>%
  filter(skim_name %in% skim$name)   # keep NILs that have a Skim-RTI call (so a pick is always paintable)
ms <- mean(cov$skim_cov); mb <- mean(cov$brb_cov)
cat(sprintf("%d pedigree-matched NILs | mean coverage: SNP50K skim %.3f× | BRB-seq %.3f×\n",
            nrow(cov), ms, mb))
334 pedigree-matched NILs | mean coverage: SNP50K skim 0.434× | BRB-seq 2.811×

Coverage-matched series — grid the varying platform across its central 95%

To sweep one platform’s coverage while controlling the other, we grid the varying platform across its central 95% (P2.5–P97.5) on 10 evenly-spaced steps; at each step we take the NIL nearest the intersection of that grid line and the held platform’s mean, measuring distance in the plot’s screen space (each coverage axis scaled by its plotted span, ≈ 10:1 skim:BRB). This pins picks to both the evenly-spaced grid and the held-mean line (feasible because the two coverages are uncorrelated). The screen weight was calibrated against hand-clicked picks on the skim sweep (reproduces 9/10).

Code 
# At each of the n grid steps, pick the NIL nearest the INTERSECTION of (grid_target on the
# varying axis, hold_mean on the held axis), with distance measured in *screen* space — each
# coverage axis scaled by its plotted span (weights `W`; BRB spans ~10× skim's range). This
# lands picks on both the evenly-spaced grid and the held-mean line. Calibrated to reproduce
# hand-clicked picks on the skim sweep (9/10); generalises to the BRB sweep by swapping which
# axis carries the grid (the weights make it symmetric).
W <- c(skim_cov = 1, brb_cov = 0.1)   # per-unit screen weight (skim:BRB ≈ 10:1)
grid_series <- function(df, vary, hold, hold_mean, n = 10, q = c(0.025, 0.975)) {
  v <- df[[vary]]; h <- df[[hold]]; wv <- W[[vary]]; wh <- W[[hold]]
  gr <- seq(quantile(v, q[1]), quantile(v, q[2]), length.out = n)
  chosen <- integer(0)
  for (g in gr) {
    free <- setdiff(seq_along(v), chosen)
    D <- (wv * (v[free] - g))^2 + (wh * (h[free] - hold_mean))^2   # screen-space dist to (g, hold_mean)
    chosen <- c(chosen, free[which.min(D)])
  }
  df[chosen, , drop = FALSE] %>% mutate(grid_target = gr)
}
vary_brb  <- grid_series(cov, "brb_cov",  "skim_cov", ms)   # sweep BRB-seq, hold skim ≈ mean
vary_skim <- grid_series(cov, "skim_cov", "brb_cov", mb)    # sweep skim,    hold BRB  ≈ mean
cat(sprintf("BRB-seq central 95%%: [%.2f, %.2f]× | skim central 95%%: [%.3f, %.3f]×\n",
            quantile(cov$brb_cov,.025), quantile(cov$brb_cov,.975),
            quantile(cov$skim_cov,.025), quantile(cov$skim_cov,.975)))
BRB-seq central 95%: [1.19, 5.06]× | skim central 95%: [0.176, 0.778]×

Scatter — mean lines + the two gridded series

Code 
cov2 <- cov %>% mutate(series = case_when(
  nil %in% vary_brb$nil & nil %in% vary_skim$nil ~ "both series",
  nil %in% vary_brb$nil  ~ "vary BRB (skim≈mean)",
  nil %in% vary_skim$nil ~ "vary skim (BRB≈mean)",
  TRUE ~ "other"))
ggplot(cov2, aes(skim_cov, brb_cov)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = ms, linetype = "dotted") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = mb, linetype = "dotted") +
  geom_point(aes(colour = series, size = series == "other"), alpha = 0.8) +
  scale_size_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = 1.3, `FALSE` = 2.7), guide = "none") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(other = "grey75", `vary BRB (skim≈mean)` = "firebrick",
                                 `vary skim (BRB≈mean)` = "royalblue3", `both series` = "purple3"),
                      name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "SNP50K skim mean coverage (×)", y = "BRB-seq mean coverage (×)",
       title = "Per-NIL coverage — SNP50K skim vs BRB-seq",
       subtitle = sprintf("dotted = platform mean (skim %.2f×, BRB %.2f×) | 10-point grid across each varying platform's central 95%%",
                          ms, mb)) +
  theme_bw()

Read: BRB-seq (3′ RNA-seq) mean depth (~2.8×) sits well above the ~0.4× SNP50K skim, and the two platforms’ coverages are uncorrelated across NILs (library-driven). Each series steps one platform evenly across its central-95% coverage while holding the other ≈ its mean — a coverage-controlled sweep for asking how the ancestry calls move with the varying platform’s depth, with the other platform’s coverage held out as a confounder.

Coverage-sweep chromosome painting

Ancestry calls for the two 10-NIL coverage sweeps, painted as the coverage of the varying platform climbs (rows ordered low→high; the row label prefixes the varying λ). Three tracks per NIL — top→bottom = Skim-RTI (r=5), nilHMM (counts), BrB-RTI (r=7, ws) — and a B73 control row pinned at top (forced, not pedigree-matched: skim PN10_SID893, BRB PN3_SID213 — clean reps; the old PN1_SID15 is an introgressed impostor, docs/b73_checks_qc.html). Each B73 control comes from its platform’s B73 check group, fit separately from the teosinte donors.

Clean-control note. The BrB-seq B73 control is PN3_SID213 (≈ 0 donor genome-wide). The plate-labeled PN1_SID15 used previously is an introgressed impostor — 6 of the 35 BrB-seq “B73” reps carry real localized donor (all on plate PN1), a BRB-seq labeling artifact; skim/MolB B73 are clean. Per-experiment recommended clean controls: B73 check QC.

BrB-RTI = wideseq-filtered, per-species, r=7. BRB-seq 3′ markers are dense and noisy, so on the full joint-called SNP set RTIGER needed an extreme rigidity (r=109). Restricting the BRB allele counts to the wideseq teosinte-informative positions (21,665 of 66,983 SNPs; data/brbseq_wideseq/brb_wideseq.vcf.gz, GATK SelectVariants on the Chen2022 panel) strips the off-target noise and drops the KS-calibrated rigidity to r=7 — chosen by minimizing D = sup_x|F_called − F_sim| of the donor-block size distribution vs the n=1500 BC2S3 simulation (D=0.103, vs 0.112 at the old r=109; median donor block 11.3 Mb ≈ the sim’s 10.74). Curve in results/sim_calibration/brbseq_ks_wideseq/brbseq_ks_refined.csv. BrB-RTI is fit per teosinte species (Z. mays ssp. parviglumis Zv, ssp. mexicana Zx, ssp. huehuetenangensis Zh, Z. diploperennis Zd, Z. luxurians Zl), B73 and Purple as separate checks (brbseq_taxa_r7_wideseq). The B73 check-group floor stays low (median ~0, mean ~0.05); the control PN3_SID213 reads ≈ 0 donor.

Code 
brb_sw  <- read_csv(params$brb_sweep,  show_col_types = FALSE)
skim_sw <- read_csv(params$skim_sweep, show_col_types = FALSE)
mem     <- read_csv(params$members,    show_col_types = FALSE)
BRB_B73 <- "PN3_SID213"; SKIM_B73 <- "PN10_SID893"   # clean B73 reps (PN1_SID15 is an introgressed impostor; see docs/b73_checks_qc.html)

lane2 <- function(seg, nm, method, rowlab) {
  d <- seg %>% filter(name == nm)
  if (!nrow(d)) return(NULL)
  tibble(row = rowlab, chr = d$chr, start_bp = d$start_bp, end_bp = d$end_bp,
         state = factor(d$state, 0:2, c("REF","HET","ALT")), method = method)
}
sweep_paint <- function(which) {
  m <- mem %>% filter(sweep == which) %>% arrange(vary_cov) %>%
    mutate(rowlab = sprintf("%.2f×<br>%s", vary_cov, gsub("_", "<br>", nil)))
  nil_rows <- pmap_dfr(list(m$skim_name, m$brb_name, m$rowlab), function(sk, br, rl)
    bind_rows(lane2(skim_sw, sk, "Skim-RTI", rl), lane2(nilhmm, sk, "nilHMM", rl),
              lane2(brb_sw, br, "BrB-RTI", rl)))   # nilHMM keyed on the skim sample name
  b73 <- bind_rows(lane2(skim_sw, SKIM_B73, "Skim-RTI", "**B73 control**"),
                   lane2(nilhmm_chk, SKIM_B73, "nilHMM", "**B73 control**"),  # nilHMM B73 from its check group
                   lane2(brb_sw,  BRB_B73,  "BrB-RTI",  "**B73 control**"))
  # B73 control pinned at the TOP; coverage rows keep their current descending order below
  bind_rows(b73, nil_rows) %>%
    mutate(chr = factor(chr, levels = 1:10, labels = paste0("chr", 1:10)),
           row = factor(row, levels = c("**B73 control**", rev(m$rowlab))),
           method = factor(method, c("Skim-RTI","nilHMM","BrB-RTI")),
           ylo = case_when(method == "Skim-RTI" ~ 0.68, method == "nilHMM" ~ 0.34, TRUE ~ 0.00),
           yhi = case_when(method == "Skim-RTI" ~ 1.00, method == "nilHMM" ~ 0.66, TRUE ~ 0.32))
}
paint_plot <- function(df, title, sub) {
  ggplot(df, aes(xmin = start_bp/1e6, xmax = end_bp/1e6, ymin = ylo, ymax = yhi, fill = state)) +
    geom_rect() +
    facet_grid(row ~ chr, scales = "free_x", space = "free_x", switch = "y") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = pal, drop = FALSE) +
    scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::unit_format(unit = "", scale = 1)) +
    scale_y_continuous(breaks = c(0.16, 0.50, 0.84), labels = c("BrB-RTI","nilHMM","Skim-RTI"),
                       expand = expansion(mult = 0.02), position = "right") +
    labs(title = title, subtitle = sub, x = "Position (Mb)", fill = "Genotype") +
    ggpubr::theme_classic2(base_size = 9) +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom", strip.background = element_blank(),
          strip.text.x = element_text(face = "bold"),
          strip.text.y.left = ggtext::element_markdown(angle = 0, hjust = 1, size = 9, lineheight = 0.8),
          panel.spacing.x = unit(0.05, "lines"), panel.spacing.y = unit(0.18, "lines"),
          axis.text.y.right = element_text(size = 9), axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
          axis.title.y = element_blank(), axis.line.y = element_blank(),
          axis.text.x = element_text(size = 6))
}

Pedigree-matched pairs

Code 
jac_one <- function(s_nil) {
  p <- matched[matched$nil == s_nil, ]
  b <- state_on_grid(brb,  p$brb_name); k <- state_on_grid(skim, p$skim_name)
  h <- state_on_grid(nilhmm, p$skim_name)               # nilHMM, same skim sample
  ok <- !is.na(b) & !is.na(k); bd <- b[ok] > 0; kd <- k[ok] > 0; u <- sum(bd | kd)
  okh <- !is.na(h) & !is.na(k); hd <- h[okh] > 0; kdh <- k[okh] > 0; uh <- sum(hd | kdh)
  tibble(donor_J    = if (u == 0)  NA_real_ else sum(bd & kd)/u,        # Skim-RTI vs BrB-RTI
         J_skim_nil = if (uh == 0) NA_real_ else sum(hd & kdh)/uh,      # Skim-RTI vs nilHMM (same reads)
         concord = mean(b[ok] == k[ok]),
         brb_donor = mean(bd), skim_donor = mean(kd), nil_donor = mean(h[!is.na(h)] > 0))
}
pair_tab <- matched %>% mutate(m = map(nil, jac_one)) %>% unnest(m) %>%
  transmute(NIL = nil, brb_label = brb_name, skim_sample = skim_name,
            donor_J = round(donor_J, 2), J_skim_nil = round(J_skim_nil, 2), concord = round(concord, 3),
            brb_donor = round(brb_donor, 3), skim_donor = round(skim_donor, 3), nil_donor = round(nil_donor, 3)) %>%
  arrange(desc(donor_J))
knitr::kable(pair_tab,
             caption = "Per pedigree-matched NIL: donor Jaccard Skim-RTI vs BrB-RTI (donor_J) and Skim-RTI vs nilHMM (J_skim_nil, same-reads check), marker concordance, and per-caller donor fraction. (PN#_SID# plate labels for provenance only.)")
Per pedigree-matched NIL: donor Jaccard Skim-RTI vs BrB-RTI (donor_J) and Skim-RTI vs nilHMM (J_skim_nil, same-reads check), marker concordance, and per-caller donor fraction. (PN#_SID# plate labels for provenance only.)

Read: high donor_J = the two platforms agree on where the teosinte is for that NIL. A low value where the pedigree matches but the genotype doesn’t (watch Zx.0370) flags a sample whose BRB-seq content disagrees with its stated pedigree — a residual identity problem beyond the .B fix.

Confusion matrices — pairwise (pooled, matched NILs)

Code 
paired <- map_dfr(matched$nil, function(s_nil) {
  p <- matched[matched$nil == s_nil, ]
  tibble(nil  = s_nil,
         skim = state_on_grid(skim,   p$skim_name),
         brb  = state_on_grid(brb,    p$brb_name),
         nilh = state_on_grid(nilhmm, p$skim_name))   # nilHMM, same skim sample
})
cats <- c("0 recurrent","1 het","2 donor")
cm_kable <- function(rows, cols, rlab, clab) {
  ok <- !is.na(rows) & !is.na(cols)
  cm <- table(factor(rows[ok], 0:2), factor(cols[ok], 0:2))
  prop <- sweep(cm, 1, rowSums(cm), "/")
  disp <- matrix(sprintf("%d (%.1f%%)", cm, 100*prop), nrow = 3, dimnames = list(cats, cats))
  knitr::kable(disp, align = "r",
               caption = sprintf("%s (rows) vs %s (cols): count (row %%). Overall concordance %.3f.",
                                 rlab, clab, sum(diag(cm))/sum(cm)))
}

Introgression-size distribution

Donor-block sizes (runs of donor state — HET or ALT — collapsed per chromosome) pooled across the full set of NILs called on both platforms (pedigree-matched via the correspondence; BrB-RTI from the per-species fit, all teosinte species). Grey curve is the Null n=1500 BC2S3 simulation — the modeled expectation under no selection.

Code 
brb_taxa <- read_csv(params$brb_taxa, show_col_types = FALSE)   # full per-species BrB-RTI (379)
nil_seg  <- read_csv(params$nil_seg,  show_col_types = FALSE)   # n=1500 sim (NULL)

# FULL set of NILs with calls on BOTH platforms (pedigree-matched, ";"-split replicates)
brb_in  <- corr %>% separate_rows(brbseq_prefix, sep = ";") %>%
  transmute(name = brbseq_prefix, nil = pedigree) %>% filter(name %in% brb_taxa$name)
skim_in <- corr %>% separate_rows(skim_prefix,  sep = ";") %>%
  transmute(name = skim_prefix,  nil = pedigree) %>% filter(name %in% skim$name)
both_nils <- intersect(brb_in$nil, skim_in$nil)

# introgression block = maximal run of donor (state>0) within a (sample, chromosome)
donor_blocks <- function(seg) seg %>% arrange(name, chr, start_bp) %>% group_by(name, chr) %>%
  mutate(run = cumsum(c(TRUE, diff(state > 0) != 0)), donor = state > 0) %>% filter(donor) %>%
  group_by(name, chr, run) %>% summarise(size_mb = (max(end_bp) - min(start_bp))/1e6, .groups = "drop")

skim_b <- donor_blocks(skim     %>% filter(name %in% skim_in$name[skim_in$nil %in% both_nils])) %>%
  mutate(src = "Skim-RTI (r=5)")
brb_b  <- donor_blocks(brb_taxa %>% filter(name %in% brb_in$name[brb_in$nil  %in% both_nils])) %>%
  mutate(src = "BrB-RTI (r=7, ws)")
# nilHMM on the SAME skim samples (keyed on skim name)
nil_b  <- donor_blocks(nilhmm   %>% filter(name %in% skim_in$name[skim_in$nil %in% both_nils])) %>%
  mutate(src = "nilHMM (counts)")
null_b <- nil_seg %>% transmute(size_mb = mb)
cat(sprintf("NILs called on both platforms: %d | Skim %d blocks | BrB %d blocks | nilHMM %d blocks\n",
            length(both_nils), nrow(skim_b), nrow(brb_b), nrow(nil_b)))
NILs called on both platforms: 332 | Skim 1915 blocks | BrB 2846 blocks | nilHMM 1831 blocks
Code 
ggplot(bind_rows(skim_b, brb_b, nil_b), aes(x = size_mb, fill = src)) +
  geom_histogram(aes(y = after_stat(density)), position = "identity", alpha = 0.45, bins = 30) +
  geom_freqpoly(data = null_b, aes(x = size_mb, y = after_stat(density)),
                bins = 30, colour = "grey20", linewidth = 0.9, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Skim-RTI (r=5)" = "purple4", "BrB-RTI (r=7, ws)" = "orange3",
                               "nilHMM (counts)" = "steelblue")) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  labs(x = "introgression size (Mb, log scale)", y = "density", fill = NULL,
       title = "Introgression-size distribution — Skim-RTI / BrB-RTI / nilHMM",
       subtitle = sprintf("%d NILs called on both platforms (pedigree-matched, full set) | grey = Null (n=1500 sim)",
                          length(both_nils))) +
  theme_bw()

Chromosome painting — Skim-RTI / BrB-RTI / nilHMM per NIL

Three tracks per NIL (top→bottom = Skim-RTI r=5, nilHMM counts, BrB-RTI r=7 wideseq), grouped and labelled by the .B-dropped pedigree (wrapped at the left); the method label is at the right. NILs ordered by Skim-RTI vs BrB-RTI donor Jaccard (best agreement first).

Code 
nil_ord <- pair_tab$NIL
lane <- function(seg, nm, method, s_nil) {
  d <- seg[seg$name == nm, ]
  tibble(nil = s_nil, chr = d$chr, start_bp = d$start_bp, end_bp = d$end_bp,
         state = factor(d$state, 0:2, c("REF","HET","ALT")), method = method)
}
paint <- map_dfr(matched$nil, function(s_nil) {
  p <- matched[matched$nil == s_nil, ]
  bind_rows(lane(skim,   p$skim_name, "Skim-RTI", s_nil),
            lane(nilhmm, p$skim_name, "nilHMM",   s_nil),    # same skim sample
            lane(brb,    p$brb_name,  "BrB-RTI",  s_nil))
}) %>%
  mutate(chr  = factor(chr, levels = 1:10, labels = paste0("chr", 1:10)),
         nil  = factor(gsub("_", "<br>", nil), levels = gsub("_", "<br>", nil_ord)),
         method = factor(method, c("Skim-RTI","nilHMM","BrB-RTI")),
         ylo = case_when(method == "Skim-RTI" ~ 0.68, method == "nilHMM" ~ 0.34, TRUE ~ 0.00),
         yhi = case_when(method == "Skim-RTI" ~ 1.00, method == "nilHMM" ~ 0.66, TRUE ~ 0.32))

ggplot(paint, aes(xmin = start_bp/1e6, xmax = end_bp/1e6, ymin = ylo, ymax = yhi, fill = state)) +
  geom_rect() +
  facet_grid(nil ~ chr, scales = "free_x", space = "free_x", switch = "y") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = pal, drop = FALSE) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::unit_format(unit = "", scale = 1)) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = c(0.16, 0.50, 0.84), labels = c("BrB-RTI","nilHMM","Skim-RTI"),
                     expand = expansion(mult = 0.02), position = "right") +
  labs(title = "Skim-RTI / BrB-RTI / nilHMM — pedigree-matched NILs",
       subtitle = "per NIL, top→bottom: Skim-RTI (r=5) / nilHMM (counts) / BrB-RTI (r=7, ws) | gold REF, green HET, purple ALT",
       x = "Position (Mb)", fill = "Genotype") +
  ggpubr::theme_classic2(base_size = 9) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", strip.background = element_blank(),
        strip.text.x = element_text(face = "bold"),
        strip.text.y.left = ggtext::element_markdown(angle = 0, hjust = 1, size = 9, lineheight = 0.85),
        panel.spacing.x = unit(0.05, "lines"), panel.spacing.y = unit(0.15, "lines"),
        axis.text.y.right = element_text(size = 9), axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
        axis.title.y = element_blank(), axis.line.y = element_blank(),
        axis.text.x = element_text(size = 6))

Findings

  • The per-NIL painting, confusion, and Jaccard cover the 4 MolBreeding-GBTS NILs that also have BRB-seq (Zv.0080, Zx.0340, Zx.0540, Zd.0030; matched by pedigree) — the lines with the most cross-platform support. Coverage and introgression-size use the full skim∩BRB set.
  • Where the pedigrees genuinely correspond, Skim-RTI and BrB-RTI agree on the donor landscape (high donor Jaccard); BrB-RTI is the sparser, noisier track (low coverage RNA).
  • nilHMM (same skim reads, count-based BetaBinomial HMM) is the closest track to Skim-RTI — J_skim_nil and the Skim-RTI×nilHMM confusion isolate a two-implementations difference on identical reads. At ~0.4× it is het-biased, so its donor footprint is the reliable quantity, not the HET-vs-ALT split.
  • Any matched NIL with low Jaccard (e.g. Zx.0370) is a sample whose BRB-seq genotype disagrees with its stated pedigree — a residual identity issue the .B fix does not resolve, to be confirmed by the Hazel rerun (docs/brbseq-sample-mislabeling.md). ```
